sanskrit: dvābhyāṃ jāto hi mātṛbhyām ardhadehaḥ pṛthak pṛthak tayā sa saṃdhito yasmāj jarāsaṃdhas tataḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Born of two mothers, his body in two halves, each apart from the other, he was joined together by her—and because she joined him, he is remembered as Jarāsaṃdha.

sanskrit: sā tu bhūmigatā pārtha hatā sasutabāndhavā gadayā tena cāstreṇa sthūṇākarṇena rākṣasī
english: And that rākṣasī, brought down to the earth, O Pārtha, was slain together with her sons and kinsmen by that mace and by the weapon Sthūṇākarṇa.

sanskrit: vinābhūtaḥ sa gadayā jarāsaṃdho mahāmṛdhe nihato bhīmasenena paśyatas te dhanaṃjaya
english: Deprived thus of his mace, Jarāsaṃdha in the great battle was slain by Bhīmasena before your very eyes, O Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: yadi hi syād gadāpāṇir jarāsaṃdhaḥ pratāpavān sendrā devā na taṃ hantuṃ raṇe śaktā narottama
english: For had the mighty Jarāsaṃdha held the mace in his hand, the gods themselves with Indra would not have been able to slay him in battle, O best of men.

sanskrit: tvaddhitārthaṃ hi naiṣādir aṅguṣṭhena viyojitaḥ droṇenācāryakaṃ kṛtvā chadmanā satyavikramaḥ
english: It was for your sake that the Niṣāda's son, of true valor, was parted from his thumb—when, by a stratagem, he had made Droṇa his teacher.

sanskrit: sa tu baddhāṅgulitrāṇo naiṣādir dṛḍhavikramaḥ asyann eko vanacaro babhau rāma ivāparaḥ
english: That son of the Niṣāda, of firm valor, his finger-guard bound on, shooting alone, a forest-dweller, shone like a second Rāma.

sanskrit: ekalavyaṃ hi sāṅguṣṭham aśaktā devadānavāḥ sarākṣasoragāḥ pārtha vijetuṃ yudhi karhi cit
english: For with his thumb intact, Ekalavya could never have been vanquished in battle, O Pārtha, by gods or dānavas, by rākṣasas or serpents.

sanskrit: kim u mānuṣamātreṇa śakyaḥ syāt prativīkṣitum dṛḍhamuṣṭiḥ kṛtī nityam asyamāno divāniśam
english: How then could a mere mortal even dare to look upon him—firm of grip, accomplished, ever shooting his shafts by day and by night?

sanskrit: tvaddhitārthaṃ tu sa mayā hataḥ saṃgrāmamūrdhani cedirājaś ca vikrāntaḥ pratyakṣaṃ nihatas tava
english: For your sake he was slain by me at the forefront of battle; and the valiant king of the Cedis was struck down before your very eyes.

sanskrit: sa cāpy aśakyaḥ saṃgrāme jetuṃ sarvaiḥ surāsuraiḥ vadhārthaṃ tasya jāto 'ham anyeṣāṃ ca suradviṣām
english: He too could not be conquered in battle by all the gods and asuras together; and it was for his slaying, and that of the other foes of the gods, that I was born.

sanskrit: tvatsahāyo naravyāghra lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā hiḍimbabakakirmīrā bhīmasenena pātitāḥ rāvaṇena samaprāṇā brahmayajñavināśanāḥ
english: As your ally, O tiger among men, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds—Hiḍimba, Baka, and Kirmīra, equal in life-force to Rāvaṇa, destroyers of the Brahmins' sacrifices, were brought low by Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: hatas tathaiva māyāvī haiḍimbenāpy alāyudhaḥ haiḍimbaś cāpy upāyena śaktyā karṇena ghātitaḥ
english: So too the sorcerer Alāyudha was slain by Hiḍimbā's son; and Hiḍimbā's son in turn, by a stratagem, was killed by Karṇa with the spear.

sanskrit: yadi hy enaṃ nāhaniṣyat karṇaḥ śaktyā mahāmṛdhe mayā vadhyo 'bhaviṣyat sa bhaimasenir ghaṭotkacaḥ
english: For had Karṇa not slain him with the spear in the great battle, that Ghaṭotkaca, Bhīmasena's son, would have had to be slain by me.

sanskrit: mayā na nihataḥ pūrvam eṣa yuṣmatpriyepsayā eṣa hi brāhmaṇadveṣī yajñadveṣī ca rākṣasaḥ
english: He was not slain by me before, out of my wish to do what was dear to you; for this rākṣasa was a hater of Brahmins and a hater of sacrifices.

sanskrit: dharmasya loptā pāpātmā tasmād eṣa nipātitaḥ vyaṃsitā cāpy upāyena śakradattā mayānagha
english: A destroyer of dharma, evil of soul—therefore he was struck down; and the spear given by Indra was, by a stratagem, made to fail, O sinless one.

sanskrit: ye hi dharmasya loptāro vadhyās te mama pāṇḍava dharmasaṃsthāpanārthaṃ hi pratijñaiṣā mamāvyayā
english: For those who would destroy dharma are to be slain by me, O Pāṇḍava; this is my imperishable vow, made for the establishment of dharma.

sanskrit: brahma satyaṃ damaḥ śaucaṃ dharmo hrīḥ śrīr dhṛtiḥ kṣamā yatra tatra rame nityam ahaṃ satyena te śape
english: Sacred knowledge, truth, self-restraint, purity, dharma, modesty, prosperity, fortitude, forbearance—wherever these are, there I ever delight: by truth I swear it to you.

sanskrit: na viṣādas tvayā kāryaḥ karṇaṃ vaikartanaṃ prati upadekṣyāmy upāyaṃ te yena taṃ prasahiṣyasi
english: You must not grieve on account of Karṇa, the son of the Sun; I will teach you the means by which you shall overcome him.

sanskrit: suyodhanaṃ cāpi raṇe haniṣyati vṛkodaraḥ tasya cāpi vadhopāyaṃ vakṣyāmi tava pāṇḍava
english: And Vṛkodara shall slay Suyodhana in battle; the means of his slaying too I will declare to you, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: vardhate tumulas tv eṣa śabdaḥ paracamūṃ prati vidravanti ca sainyāni tvadīyāni diśo daśa
english: But this tumultuous din swells against the enemy's host, and your own troops are scattering in flight to the ten directions.

sanskrit: labdhalakṣyā hi kauravyā vidhamanti camūṃ tava dahaty eṣa ca vaḥ sainyaṃ droṇaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ
english: For the Kauravas, having found their mark, are shattering your army; and Droṇa, best of strikers, is burning down your forces.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ekavīravadhe moghā śaktiḥ sūtātmaje yadā kasmāt sarvān samutsṛjya sa tāṃ pārthe na muktavān
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When the spear of the Sūta's son was wasted upon the slaying of a single hero, why, passing over all the rest, did he not hurl it at Pārtha?

sanskrit: tasmin hate hatā hi syuḥ sarve pāṇḍavasṛñjayāḥ ekavīravadhe kasmān na yuddhe jayam ādadhat
english: For with him slain, all the Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas would have been slain; why, by the slaying of that one hero, did he not seize victory in the war?

sanskrit: āhūto na nivarteyam iti tasya mahāvratam svayam āhvayitavyaḥ sa sūtaputreṇa phalgunaḥ
english: "Once challenged, I will not turn back"—such was Phalguna's great vow; therefore the Sūta's son had only to challenge him himself.

sanskrit: tato dvairatham ānīya phalgunaṃ śakradattayā na jaghāna vṛṣā kasmāt tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Then, having drawn Phalguna into a chariot-duel, why did the bull-like Karṇa not slay him with Indra's gift? Tell me that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: nūnaṃ buddhivihīnaś cāpy asahāyaś ca me sutaḥ śatrubhir vyaṃsitopāyaḥ kathaṃ nu sa jayed arīn
english: Surely my son is bereft of wisdom and without true allies; his designs thwarted by his foes—how then could he ever conquer his enemies?

sanskrit: yā hy asya paramā śaktir jayasya ca parāyaṇam sā śaktir vāsudevena vyaṃsitāsya ghaṭotkace
english: For that supreme spear of his, the very mainstay of his victory—that spear was made by Vāsudeva to be spent upon Ghaṭotkaca.

sanskrit: kuṇer yathā hastagataṃ hriyed bilvaṃ balīyasā tathā śaktir amoghā sā moghībhūtā ghaṭotkace
english: As a bilva fruit in the hand of a crippled man is snatched away by one stronger, so that unfailing spear was made to fail upon Ghaṭotkaca.

sanskrit: yathā varāhasya śunaś ca yudhyatos; tayor abhāve śvapacasya lābhaḥ manye vidvan vāsudevasya tadvad; yuddhe lābhaḥ karṇahaiḍimbayor vai
english: As when a boar and a dog fight and, both being destroyed, the dog-eater gains the spoil—so too, O learned one, I deem it was Vāsudeva who gained from the combat of Karṇa and Hiḍimbā's son.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkaco yadi hanyād dhi karṇaṃ; paro lābhaḥ sa bhavet pāṇḍavānām vaikartano vā yadi taṃ nihanyāt; tathāpi kṛtyaṃ śaktināśāt kṛtaṃ syāt
english: For if Ghaṭotkaca should slay Karṇa, that would be the greater gain for the Pāṇḍavas; and if the son of the Sun should slay him, even so the purpose would be achieved through the loss of the spear.

sanskrit: iti prājñaḥ prajñayaitad vicārya; ghaṭotkacaṃ sūtaputreṇa yuddhe ayodhayad vāsudevo nṛsiṃhaḥ; priyaṃ kurvan pāṇḍavānāṃ hitaṃ ca
english: Thus the wise Vāsudeva, lion among men, having weighed this in his wisdom, set Ghaṭotkaca to fight the Sūta's son in battle, doing what was dear and beneficial to the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca etac cikīrṣitaṃ jñātvā karṇe madhunihā nṛpa niyojayām āsa tadā dvairathe rākṣaseśvaram
english: Saṃjaya said: Knowing this intent in Karṇa, O king, the slayer of Madhu then set the lord of the rākṣasas to the chariot-duel.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkacaṃ mahāvīryaṃ mahābuddhir janārdanaḥ amoghāyā vighātārthaṃ rājan durmantrite tava
english: The deeply wise Janārdana set mighty Ghaṭotkaca to draw forth the unfailing spear, O king—amid your evil counsels.

sanskrit: tadaiva kṛtakāryā hi vayaṃ syāma kurūdvaha na rakṣed yadi kṛṣṇas taṃ pārthaṃ karṇān mahārathāt
english: Then indeed our purpose would have been accomplished, O scion of Kuru, had Kṛṣṇa not been guarding that Pārtha from Karṇa, the great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: sāśvadhvajarathaḥ saṃkhye dhṛtarāṣṭra pated bhuvi vinā janārdanaṃ pārtho yogānām īśvaraṃ prabhum
english: With his horses, his banner, and his chariot, O Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pārtha would have fallen to the earth in battle—but for Janārdana, the lord and master of all yogas.

sanskrit: tais tair upāyair bahubhī rakṣyamāṇaḥ sa pārthiva jayaty abhimukhaḥ śatrūn pārthaḥ kṛṣṇena pālitaḥ
english: Guarded by those many devices, O king, Pārtha, protected by Kṛṣṇa, conquers his foes face to face.

sanskrit: saviśeṣaṃ tv amoghāyāḥ kṛṣṇo 'rakṣata pāṇḍavam hanyāt kṣiptā hi kaunteyaṃ śaktir vṛkṣam ivāśaniḥ
english: But it was above all from the unfailing spear that Kṛṣṇa guarded the Pāṇḍava; for that spear, once hurled, would have struck down Kuntī's son as a thunderbolt fells a tree.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca virodhī ca kumantrī ca prājñamānī mamātmajaḥ yasyaiṣa samatikrānto vadhopāyo jayaṃ prati
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: A maker of strife, ill in counsel, and yet deeming himself wise is my son—he for whom this means of slaying, the path to victory, has been let slip.

sanskrit: tavāpi samatikrāntam etad gāvalgaṇe katham etam arthaṃ mahābuddhe yat tvayā nāvabodhitaḥ
english: And how was this let slip by you too, O son of Gavalgaṇa—that you, O deeply wise one, did not make this matter understood?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca duryodhanasya śakuner mama duḥśāsanasya ca rātrau rātrau bhavaty eṣā nityam eva samarthanā
english: Saṃjaya said: Night after night, this very counsel was urged, ever and again, by Duryodhana, by Śakuni, by me, and by Duḥśāsana:

sanskrit: śvaḥ sarvasainyān utsṛjya jahi karṇa dhanaṃjayam preṣyavat pāṇḍupāñcālān upabhokṣyāmahe tataḥ
english: "Tomorrow, Karṇa, leave aside all the troops and slay Dhanaṃjaya; then shall we make the Pāṇḍus and Pāñcālas serve us like menials."

sanskrit: atha vā nihate pārthe pāṇḍuṣv anyatamaṃ tataḥ sthāpayed yudhi vārṣṇeyas tasmāt kṛṣṇo nipātyatām
english: "Or else, with Pārtha slain, the Vārṣṇeya would set up some other among the Pāṇḍus in the fight; therefore let Kṛṣṇa be struck down."

sanskrit: kṛṣṇo hi mūlaṃ pāṇḍūnāṃ pārthaḥ skandha ivodgataḥ śākhā ivetare pārthāḥ pāñcālāḥ patrasaṃjñitāḥ
english: "For Kṛṣṇa is the root of the Pāṇḍus, and Pārtha is the trunk risen up; the other sons of Pṛthā are as the branches, and the Pāñcālas may be called the leaves."

sanskrit: kṛṣṇāśrayāḥ kṛṣṇabalāḥ kṛṣṇanāthāś ca pāṇḍavāḥ kṛṣṇaḥ parāyaṇaṃ caiṣāṃ jyotiṣām iva candramāḥ
english: "The Pāṇḍavas have Kṛṣṇa for their refuge, Kṛṣṇa for their strength, Kṛṣṇa for their lord; Kṛṣṇa is their supreme recourse, as the moon among the lights of heaven."

sanskrit: tasmāt parṇāni śākhāś ca skandhaṃ cotsṛjya sūtaja kṛṣṇaṃ nikṛndhi pāṇḍūnāṃ mūlaṃ sarvatra sarvadā
english: "Therefore, son of the Sūta, leaving aside the leaves, the branches, and the trunk, cut down Kṛṣṇa, the root of the Pāṇḍus, everywhere and always."

sanskrit: hanyād yadi hi dāśārhaṃ karṇo yādavanandanam kṛtsnā vasumatī rājan vaśe te syān na saṃśayaḥ
english: "For if Karṇa should slay the Dāśārha, the joy of the Yādavas, then the whole earth, O king, would fall under your sway—of that there is no doubt."

sanskrit: yadi hi sa nihataḥ śayīta bhūmau; yadukulapāṇḍavanandano mahātmā nanu tava vasudhā narendra sarvā; sagirisamudravanā vaśaṃ vrajeta
english: "For if that great soul, the joy of the Yadu line and of the Pāṇḍavas, were slain and lay upon the earth, then surely, O lord of men, the whole world, with its mountains, seas, and forests, would pass under your sway."

sanskrit: sā tu buddhiḥ kṛtāpy evaṃ jāgrati tridaśeśvare aprameye hṛṣīkeśe yuddhakāle vyamuhyata
english: But this resolve, though so taken, faltered in the hour of battle, while the immeasurable Hṛṣīkeśa, lord of the thirty gods, kept watch.

sanskrit: arjunaṃ cāpi kaunteyaṃ sadā rakṣati keśavaḥ na hy enam aicchat pramukhe sauteḥ sthāpayituṃ raṇe
english: For Keśava ever guards Arjuna, the son of Kuntī; he did not wish to set him in the battle face to face with the Sūta's son.

sanskrit: anyāṃś cāsmai rathodārān upasthāpayad acyutaḥ amoghāṃ tāṃ kathaṃ śaktiṃ moghāṃ kuryām iti prabho
english: And the unfallen one set other noble chariot-warriors against him, thinking, "How may I make that unfailing spear to fail?"—O lord.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛṣṇaṃ mahābāhuḥ sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ papraccha rathaśārdūla karṇaṃ prati mahāratham
english: Then mighty-armed Sātyaki, of true valor, that tiger among chariot-warriors, asked Kṛṣṇa concerning Karṇa, the great chariot-warrior:

sanskrit: ayaṃ ca pratyayaḥ karṇe śaktyā cāmitavikrama kimarthaṃ sūtaputreṇa na muktā phalgune tu sā
english: "There was this confidence placed in Karṇa, O you of measureless valor, by reason of the spear; why then was it not loosed by the Sūta's son upon Phalguna?"

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca duḥṣāsanaś ca karṇaś ca śakuniś ca sasaindhavaḥ satataṃ mantrayanti sma duryodhanapurogamāḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: Duḥśāsana, Karṇa, and Śakuni, together with the king of the Sindhus, ever took counsel, with Duryodhana at their head:

sanskrit: karṇa karṇa maheṣvāsa raṇe 'mitaparākrama nānyasya śaktir eṣā te moktavyā jayatāṃ vara
english: "Karṇa, Karṇa, mighty archer, of measureless prowess in battle—this spear of yours must be loosed upon none other, O best of the victorious—

sanskrit: ṛte mahārathāt pārthāt kuntīputrād dhanaṃjayāt sa hi teṣām atiyaśā devānām iva vāsavaḥ
english: "—save upon the great chariot-warrior Pārtha, Dhanaṃjaya, the son of Kuntī; for he is the most glorious among them, as Vāsava among the gods."

sanskrit: tasmin vinihate sarve pāṇḍavāḥ sṛñjayaiḥ saha bhaviṣyanti gatātmānaḥ surā iva niragnayaḥ
english: "With him slain, all the Pāṇḍavas along with the Sṛñjayas will be as souls departed, like gods bereft of their sacred fires."

sanskrit: tatheti ca pratijñātaṃ karṇena śinipuṃgava hṛdi nityaṃ tu karṇasya vadho gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ
english: And "So be it" was Karṇa's pledge, O bull of the Śini line; yet ever in Karṇa's heart was the slaying of the wielder of Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: aham eva tu rādheyaṃ mohayāmi yudhāṃ vara yato nāvasṛjac chaktiṃ pāṇḍave śvetavāhane
english: But it was I myself who bewildered the son of Rādhā, O best of warriors, so that he did not loose the spear upon the Pāṇḍava of the white steeds.

sanskrit: phalgunasya hi tāṃ mṛtyum avagamya yuyutsataḥ na nidrā na ca me harṣo manaso 'sti yudhāṃ vara
english: For, knowing that spear to be the death of Phalguna who longs to fight, I have had no sleep nor any gladness of mind, O best of warriors.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkace vyaṃsitāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā tāṃ śinipuṃgava mṛtyor āsyāntarān muktaṃ paśyāmy adya dhanaṃjayam
english: But now, having seen that spear made to fail upon Ghaṭotkaca, O bull of the Śini line, I behold Dhanaṃjaya this day delivered from the very jaws of death.

sanskrit: na pitā na ca me mātā na yūyaṃ bhrātaras tathā na ca prāṇās tathā rakṣyā yathā bībhatsur āhave
english: Not my father, nor my mother, nor you, nor my brothers, nor even my own life is so to be guarded as Bībhatsu in battle.

sanskrit: trailokyarājyād yat kiṃ cid bhaved anyat sudurlabham neccheyaṃ sātvatāhaṃ tad vinā pārthaṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: Were there anything beyond the sovereignty of the three worlds, however hard to win, I would not desire it, O Sātvata, if it lacked Pārtha, Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: ataḥ praharṣaḥ sumahān yuyudhānādya me 'bhavat mṛtaṃ pratyāgatam iva dṛṣṭvā pārthaṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: Therefore a very great joy has come to me this day, O Yuyudhāna, beholding Pārtha, Dhanaṃjaya, as one returned from the dead.

sanskrit: ataś ca prahito yuddhe mayā karṇāya rākṣasaḥ na hy anyaḥ samare rātrau śaktaḥ karṇaṃ prabādhitum
english: And for this reason was the rākṣasa sent by me against Karṇa in the battle; for no other was able to press Karṇa hard in the combat by night.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca iti sātyakaye prāha tadā devakinandanaḥ dhanaṃjayahite yuktas tatpriye satataṃ rataḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Thus did the son of Devakī speak then to Sātyaki—he who was devoted to Dhanaṃjaya's welfare and ever delighted in what was dear to him.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca karṇaduryodhanādīnāṃ śakuneḥ saubalasya ca apanītaṃ mahat tāta tava caiva viśeṣataḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Great was the misjudgment of Karṇa, Duryodhana, and the rest, of Śakuni the son of Subala—and yours above all, my son.

sanskrit: yad ājānīta tāṃ śaktim ekaghnīṃ satataṃ raṇe anivāryām asahyāṃ ca devair api savāsavaiḥ
english: For you knew that spear, slayer of one alone, ever in battle unstoppable and unbearable even to the gods with Vāsava;

sanskrit: sā kimarthaṃ na karṇena pravṛtte samare purā na devakīsute muktā phalgune vāpi saṃjaya
english: why then was it not loosed by Karṇa when battle was first joined, neither upon the son of Devakī nor upon Phalguna, O Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca saṃgrāmād vinivṛttānāṃ sarveṣāṃ no viśāṃ pate rātrau kurukulaśreṣṭha mantro 'yaṃ samajāyata
english: Saṃjaya said: When all of us had withdrawn from the fighting, O lord of peoples, this counsel arose in the night, O best of the Kuru line:

sanskrit: prabhātamātre śvobhūte keśavāyārjunāya vā śaktir eṣā vimoktavyā karṇa karṇeti nityaśaḥ
english: "At the very break of day, when tomorrow comes, this spear must be loosed upon Keśava or upon Arjuna, Karṇa, Karṇa"—thus, again and again.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhātasamaye rājan karṇasya daivataiḥ anyeṣāṃ caiva yodhānāṃ sā buddhir naśyate punaḥ
english: But then, when daybreak came, O king, by the will of the gods that resolve was lost again to Karṇa and to the other warriors.

sanskrit: daivam eva paraṃ manye yat karṇo hastasaṃsthayā na jaghāna raṇe pārthaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ vā devakīsutam
english: I deem fate supreme indeed, in that Karṇa, with the spear set in his very hand, did not slay in battle either Pārtha or Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī.

sanskrit: tasya hastasthitā śaktiḥ kālarātrir ivodyatā daivopahatabuddhitvān na tāṃ karṇo vimuktavān
english: That spear, resting in his hand, raised aloft like the Night of Doom—because his judgment was struck down by fate, Karṇa did not loose it.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇe vā devakīputre mohito devamāyayā pārthe vā śakrakalpe vai vadhārthaṃ vāsavīṃ prabho
english: Bewildered by the gods' own magic, he loosed not Vāsava's spear, O lord, for the slaying of Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī, nor of Pārtha, the peer of Śakra.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca daivenaiva hatā yūyaṃ svabuddhyā keśavasya ca gatā hi vāsavī hatvā tṛṇabhūtaṃ ghaṭotkacam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: By fate alone were you undone, and by your own judgment, and by Keśava's; for Vāsava's spear was spent in slaying Ghaṭotkaca, who was but as a blade of grass.

sanskrit: karṇaś ca mama putrāś ca sarve cānye ca pārthivāḥ anena duṣpraṇītena gatā vaivasvatakṣayam
english: And Karṇa, and my sons, and all the other kings as well, by this ill-conceived design have gone to the abode of Vaivasvata.

sanskrit: bhūya eva tu me śaṃsa yathā yuddham avartata kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca haiḍimbe nihate tadā
english: But tell me yet again how the battle of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas went forward then, when Hiḍimbā's son had been slain.

sanskrit: ye ca te 'bhyadravan droṇaṃ vyūḍhānīkāḥ prahāriṇaḥ sṛñjayāḥ saha pāñcālais te 'py akurvan kathaṃ raṇam
english: And those striking warriors who charged upon Droṇa in ordered ranks—the Sṛñjayas together with the Pāñcālas—how too did they wage the fight?

sanskrit: saumadatter vadhād droṇam āyastaṃ saindhavasya ca amarṣāj jīvitaṃ tyaktvā gāhamānaṃ varūthinīm
english: Droṇa, made fierce by the slaying of Somadatta's son and of the Sindhu king, casting away his very life in his fury, plunging into the host—

sanskrit: jṛmbhamāṇam iva vyāghraṃ vyāttānanam ivāntakam kathaṃ pratyudyayur droṇam asyantaṃ pāṇḍusṛñjayāḥ
english: —like a tiger stretching itself, like Death with jaws agape: how did the Pāṇḍus and Sṛñjayas advance against Droṇa as he loosed his shafts?
